inputs.share_count_basis: FY2026 diluted weighted-average count from the FY2026 10-K (146.054M; Q3 FY26 145.7M). Held FLAT: SBC is fully expensed in the flows, so diluting as well would double-charge it. The ~$1.5B FY2027 buyback/ASR is value-neutral in this model and is not used to shrink the count.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2026 10-K (SEC XBRL): cash-flow SBC add-back $104.348M + taxes paid on net-share settlement of equity awards $21.833M (financing). ResMed publishes no combined reconciliation figure, so the two lines are summed.
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows. Risk-free ~4.3% (10y UST), ERP 5.0%, levered beta ~0.8 for a low-leverage medical-device leader (net cash, D/E ~0.06) -> cost of equity ~8.3%; debt is immaterial so WACC ~ cost of equity, rounded to 8.5%. Same WACC in every scenario: risk is carried in the driver paths and weights, not a premium.
inputs.lease_treatment: US GAAP ASC 842: operating lease cost sits inside operating expenses and therefore inside EBITDA, so leases are already charged in the flows; lease liabilities are NOT added to net debt (one treatment only).
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF component DCF (routing table row 1: profitable US operating company, medical devices + recurring consumables + SaaS). First valuation of RMD, no prior DCF and no memory entry. Owner FCF FY2026 = reported FCF 1,649.5 - SBC incl. equity-award taxes 126.2 = 1,523.4. Interest income NOT stripped: net cash (1,070) is below 1x the FCF base, and the debt-interest paid inside OCF broadly offsets the interest earned on the cash pile. FY0 revenue includes MatrixCare/HealthcareFirst/Citus Health, sold to Frazier Healthcare in Sept 2026 for ~$490M; the FY2027 growth step (2.6%, guidance midpoint $5.80B) therefore embeds the divestiture, and the $490M proceeds (received after the 30-Jun-26 balance sheet) are added in the equity bridge. Buybacks: a repurchaser ($700M FY26, ~$1.5B guided FY27 incl. ASR) - the flat count is genuinely funded, several times over SBC. Adj. EBITDA margin anchor = (GAAP operating income 1,886.7 + D&A 201.3 + SBC 104.3) / revenue = 38.8% FY26. Capex FY26 2.8% of revenue (FY24-25 1.7-2.1%). Cash tax FY26 357/OI 1,887 = ~19%. Working capital is a manufacturer/distributor use of cash: capture -8% of the revenue increase.

equity_bridge.note: Closed Sept 2026 after the 30-Jun-26 balance sheet; ~$490M per company announcement (Analysis JSON recent_developments). Treated as untaxed: sold below the 2019 ~$750M MatrixCare purchase price, so no material gain.

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR (17.9%) diverges >30% from revenue 5yr CAGR (12.1%). Book value compounds on ~75% earnings retention and margin expansion (EBITDA margin 33% -> 37%), not on a repeatable growth rate; revenue is the more honest forward proxy, so it is selected. EPS 5yr (26.2%) starts from a tax-depressed FY2021.
historical_growth.notes: FCF CAGRs are on the owner-FCF series (reported FCF - SBC - equity-award taxes). Owner-FCF CAGR is ABOVE reported: SBC (~2% of revenue) grew slower than cash flow, so SBC is not eating the growth. The 3yr FCF CAGR starts from a FY2023 working-capital trough (inventory build post Philips recall) and overstates the run-rate.

base.narrative: FY27 at guidance midpoint ($5.80B, MatrixCare out), then high-single-digit underlying growth fading to 3.5% by year 10; margin +40bp/yr to a 40.5% adj. EBITDA plateau per guided gross-margin expansion.

bull.narrative: Top of FY27 guidance, then GLP-1 screening lifts new-patient starts and resupply into ~9% growth; mask mix and productivity carry adj. EBITDA margin to 42.5%.

bear.narrative: FY27 misses the guidance floor; Philips re-enters the US with price, reimbursement tightens and GLP-1 trims new diagnoses over time: ~3% growth and adj. EBITDA margin back to 36%.

scenario_narratives.base: ResMed delivers its FY2027 guide ($5.75-5.85B; the low reported number is the MatrixCare divestiture plus FX, not a demand stall) and then grows high-single digits as the under-diagnosed OSA pool, the AirSense 11 replacement cycle and the masks/accessories annuity on a growing installed base compound. GLP-1 proves net neutral-to-positive (ResMed's 2.5M linked-patient data), Philips rebuilds US share only slowly under its consent decree, and guided gross-margin expansion lifts adj. EBITDA margin ~170bp over five years before plateauing. Growth fades toward GDP-plus by year 10.
scenario_narratives.bull: GLP-1 becomes an outright funnel: physician screening of GLP-1 patients raises sleep-apnea diagnosis rates and CPAP initiation/compliance, while Philips stays a marginal US device supplier for years. Revenue runs ~9% in FY28-29 on top of the guided FY27 top end, the post-MatrixCare focus and mask mix take adj. EBITDA margin to ~42.5%, and the market keeps paying a 22x quality multiple at exit.
scenario_narratives.bear: Philips resolves its consent decree and re-enters the US with discounting, CMS competitive bidding and prior-authorization trim reimbursement, Astral ventilator headwinds persist, and sustained population-level GLP-1 weight loss reduces moderate OSA prevalence and new-patient device demand over the decade. Growth settles near 3%, price and mix compress adj. EBITDA margin from 38.8% to 36%, and the exit multiple de-rates to 15x as the market stops treating ResMed as a compounder.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear at 25% (above the 15% default): two credible, independent external threats - a Philips US re-entry with price and the unresolved long-run GLP-1 effect on OSA prevalence - plus payer policy risk. Base at 50%: guidance, the installed-base annuity and a net-cash balance sheet make the base path the modal outcome. Bull at 25% (below the 35% default): it needs both GLP-1 to act as a diagnosis funnel and Philips to stay sidelined, two things that must go right together.

valuation_philosophy.summary: ResMed is valued as a mature, cash-generative device-plus-consumables franchise on a strict owner-FCF basis (SBC and equity-award taxes expensed, count held flat). The valuation turns on two external axes - Philips' US re-entry and GLP-1's long-run effect on sleep-apnea prevalence - which are carried in the scenario paths and a 25% bear weight rather than in the discount rate.
key_risks_to_valuation: Philips Respironics re-entering the US device market with price after its consent decree
Long-run GLP-1 weight loss reducing OSA prevalence and new-patient device demand
Medicare competitive bidding / prior authorization compressing device and resupply reimbursement
Terminal value is ~60-70% of EV: the 20x cap multiple and 3% terminal growth carry most of the value
FX: ~42% of revenue outside the Americas
